title: Observation of dodecagonal replica bands in 30$^{\circ}$-twisted bilayer WSe$_2$
authors: Christian Valentiner-Branth Fokdal, Chakradhar Sahoo, Thomas S. Nielsen, Alfred J. H. Jones, Zhihao Jiang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Marcin Mucha-Kruczyński, Søren Ulstrup
abstract: Twisted bilayers of two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides are promising systems for achieving tunable quasicrystalline orders with emergent properties. The underpinning electronic structure and scattering processes in 2D quasicrystals with multiorbital dodecagonal replica bands have so far not been determined. Here, we utilize angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) with micrometer spatial resolution to directly observe replica bands in 30$^{\circ}$-twisted bilayer WSe$_2$. The symmetry and intensity distribution of the observed replicas are explained by interlayer Umklapp scattering from bottom to top WSe$_2$ layers. Our spectral function measurements are consistent with the presence of a van Hove singularity adjacent to the $\mathrm{K}$-valleys, which underlines the possibility of inducing electronic reconstructions in bilayers with a large interlayer twist angle.
summary: This work reports the direct observation of dodecagonal replica bands in $30^\circ$-twisted bilayer $	ext{WSe}_2$ using ARPES. By analyzing the spectral reconstruction, the authors confirm the presence of a van Hove singularity near the K-valleys. This suggests that large-angle twisted bilayer TMDs are promising platforms for inducing novel electronic states.
main_problem: The research aims to determine the electronic structure and scattering processes within 2D quasicrystals exhibiting multiorbital dodecagonal replica bands.
main_result: The authors directly observed replica bands in $30^\circ$-twisted bilayer $	ext{WSe}_2$ using ARPES, attributing them to interlayer Umklapp scattering and confirming a van Hove singularity near the K-valleys.
method: The study combines Angle-Resolved Photoemission Spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements with theoretical modeling using a two-band model to simulate the observed spectral function.
model_or_system: The physical system is $30^\circ$-twisted bilayer $	ext{WSe}_2$, which forms a quasicrystal structure. The analysis employs a two-band model to describe the hybridization and spectral reconstruction caused by interlayer coupling between the top and bottom layers.
key_observables: Direct observation of dodecagonal replica bands, spectral function measurements showing a van Hove singularity (vHs) near the K-valleys, and layer-dependent intensity asymmetries.
important_parameters: The twist angle of $30^\circ$, the energy of the vHs ($-1.05 	ext{ eV}$), and the replica band maximum energy ($-0.86 	ext{ eV}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that only states from the top and bottom valence bands mix, and that scattering processes can be modeled using first-order interlayer coupling approximations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ARPES setup and spectra along $\Gamma-	ext{K}$ cuts, showing replica bands. Other figures compare measured intensity to predictions from the two-band model, highlighting the vHs location and the effect of gap/linewidth on the spectral shape.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the physical system and the unknown electronic structure to presenting ARPES measurements confirming replica bands. It then develops a theoretical framework (two-band model) to explain the observed spectral weight transfer and the existence of the vHs.
why_interesting: The study investigates emergent electronic properties (like vHs) in engineered van der Waals heterostructures using advanced spectroscopic techniques, which is highly relevant to understanding correlated phases in low-dimensional quantum materials.
